**Exercise 3**

Choose the Electricity time series from aus_production data set of package fpp3

1. Display the time series. Do the data need transforming? If so, find a suitable transformation.

```{r}

#rm(list = ls())

library(fpp3)

elec <- aus_production |> select(Quarter, Electricity)

elec |> autoplot(Electricity)
elec |> gg_season(Electricity)

# Candidate transformations
lambda <- elec |> features(Electricity, features = guerrero) |> pull(lambda_guerrero)
lambda

elec |> autoplot(log(Electricity))
elec |> autoplot(box_cox(Electricity, lambda)) 

```

2. Are the data stationary? If not, find an appropriate differencing which yields stationary data.

```{r}
#elec <- elec |> mutate(lelec = box_cox(Electricity, lambda))
elec <- elec |> mutate(lelec = log(Electricity))

# R's suggestion
elec |> features(lelec, list(unitroot_nsdiffs, unitroot_ndiffs))

# Seasonal difference, then KPSS
elec <- elec |> mutate(d4 = difference(lelec, 4))

elec |> features(d4, unitroot_ndiffs) # we run ndiffs on the seasonally differenced series --> we get ndiffs = 1 now --> agrees with KPSS


# Add a first difference if KPSS still rejects, then test again
elec <- elec |> mutate(d4d1 = difference(d4, 1))
elec |> features(d4d1, unitroot_kpss)

elec |> autoplot(d4d1)
```

3. Identify a couple of ARIMA models that might be useful in describing the time series. Which of your models is the best according to their AIC values?

4. Compare to the result of ARIMA(). Compare the AICc and select one model.

```{r}

# ACF and PACF of the differenced log series
elec |> ACF(d4d1, lag_max = 24) |> autoplot()
elec |> PACF(d4d1, lag_max = 24) |> autoplot()

fit <- elec |>
  model(
    m1   = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(0,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,1)),
    m2   = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(0,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,2)),
    m3   = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(1,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,1)),
    auto = ARIMA(log(Electricity))
  )

# m3 = auto

fit |> select(auto) |> report()
glance(fit) |> arrange(AICc) |> select(.model, AIC, AICc, BIC)

```

5. Describe your best model and do diagnostic testing on the residuals. Do the residuals resemble white noise? If not, try to find another ARIMA model which fits better.

```{r}
# m3 has 3 coefficients (ar1, ma1, sma1), so dof = 3

fit |> select(auto) |> gg_tsresiduals()

augment(fit) |> filter(.model == "auto") |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 8, dof = 3)

```


```{r}
fit2 <- elec |>
  model(
    m3 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(1,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,1)),
    m4 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(2,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,1)),
    m5 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(1,1,2) + PDQ(0,1,1)),
    m6 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(1,1,1) + PDQ(1,1,1)),
    m7 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(1,1,1) + PDQ(0,1,2)),
    m8 = ARIMA(log(Electricity) ~ pdq(0,1,3) + PDQ(0,1,1))
  )

glance(fit2) |> arrange(AICc) |> select(.model, AIC, AICc, BIC)

fit2 |> select(m4) |> report()
fit2 |> select(m5) |> report()
```
```{r}
augment(fit2) |> filter(.model == "m4") |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 8, dof = 4)
augment(fit2) |> filter(.model == "m5") |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 8, dof = 4)


```

6. Forecast the next 24 months of data using your preferred model.

```{r}

# We will keep the model m3 --> ARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)[4]

fit |>
  select(m3) |>
  forecast(h = 8) |>
  autoplot(elec |> filter(year(Quarter) >= 1990))

fit |> select(m3) |> forecast(h = 8) |> hilo(level = 95)

```

```{r}

# We can try with m4 --> ARIMA(2,1,1)(0,1,1)[4]

fit2 |>
  select(m4) |>
  forecast(h = 8) |>
  autoplot(elec |> filter(year(Quarter) >= 1990))

fit2 |> select(m4) |> forecast(h = 8) |> hilo(level = 95)

```
